finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client created per-import in production (pool exhaustion)
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: Code constructs new PrismaClient() and only assigns it to globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production", so production code will instantiate a fresh client instead of a singleton. This creates many DB pools across serverless instances/cold starts.  
Impact: On serverless (Next.js App Router) this will exhaust Postgres connections at modest concurrent traffic causing connection pool exhaustion and immediate failures.  
Fix: Always reuse a singleton PrismaClient (assign to globalThis in all envs) and/or put the DB behind a connection pooler (PgBouncer/Neon pool) and tune pool limits.

[DB-2] Checkout flow: coupon decrement and item upserts not atomic
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: coupon is read and updated (prisma.coupon.update) before order creation and many per-item create/update/delete calls are performed outside a single transaction (existing-order path does sequential awaits in loops).  
Impact: Under concurrency this breaks idempotency and causes data inconsistency (coupon over-consumption, partial order updates) and many small writes that spike DB CPU/IOPS, leading to incorrect payments/orders at high QPS.  
Fix: Wrap coupon decrement + order create/update + all order_items mutations in a single DB transaction (batch writes where possible) and avoid sequential awaits inside loops (use bulk operations or batched tx calls).

[DB-3] Stock decrement transaction creates row-lock hotspots
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L150)
Evidence: Payment verification runs prisma.$transaction and then sequentially decrements stock per orderItem with tx.product.update / tx.productColor.update inside the transaction.  
Impact: Concurrent confirms for the same SKUs will serialize on row locks, causing heavy lock contention and slow transactions (blocking other checkouts) and cascading retries at moderate concurrency.  
Fix: Reduce transaction scope and/or batch stock updates (single UPDATE per product using SUM of quantities), use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE only on needed rows, or use optimistic reservation + background reconciliation to minimize lock duration.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded product listing queries (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L220) (also affects products/category and new-arrivals routes)
Evidence: product.findMany() is used without take/limit or cursor pagination and includes nested colors; category and new-arrivals routes do the same.  
Impact: As product count grows, these endpoints will cause full-table scans and deliver large payloads, degrading latency and DB CPU/IOPS under read-heavy traffic.  
Fix: Add pagination (cursor/limit), return only required fields, and lazy-load nested relations (or separate endpoints) to avoid scanning/transporting the entire products table.

[DB-5] Missing indexes on high‑cardinality filter/sort columns (orders/products)
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L220)
Evidence: Orders are filtered/searched by status, customerEmail, customerName and paginated with count queries, but the Order model has no indexes on status, customerEmail, customerName or createdAt; Product filtering uses category/isActive without indexes.  
Impact: Admin listing and search (prisma.order.findMany + prisma.order.count) will trigger full-table scans and slow counts once tables reach ~100k rows, causing high DB CPU and slow UI responses.  
Fix: Add targeted btree indexes (e.g., orders(status), orders(customerEmail), orders(createdAt), products(category, isActive, createdAt) or composite indexes matching the WHERE/orderBy patterns).

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Postgres chosen as datasource
File: prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: datasource provider = "postgresql".
